scenario: Accessible flood warning. Twelve residents of supported housing need a warning they can understand and act on before a flood barrier closes. Three independent teams choose recipient groups. A person contacted twice still receives only one complete warning. The residents are partitioned into numbered groups solely for this fictional table.

scenario: Urgent wage recovery. Ten migrant workers without emergency savings need a complete usable wage payment before a shelter payment deadline. Payroll can release one of three tranches, an advocate chooses verification coverage, and an access officer enables cash or account withdrawal. Releasing money alone is not usable service. Additional burdens represent exposure and mistaken debits.

The outcome values are fictional and complete, not a clinical protocol.

A power operator, care coordinator and water operator independently select local loads. Excess electrical draw trips the isolated supply. Evaporative cooling can preserve some service after a trip, with a stipulated hygiene burden.

scenario: Emergency respite allocation. Ten exhausted carers and the disabled adults they support need completed respite sessions. The setting scheduler, travel team and overnight staffing team each choose an allocation. An imbalance leaves matched capacity unusable; unfamiliar settings and overnight handoffs impose stipulated burdens. Essential support can justify limited burden where no equally effective gentler route exists.
